summary: @apexfdn/apex postinstall drops opaque binary from publisher-mismatched GitHub org
details: Package manifest, README, and homepage (omp.sh) present this as the `oh-my-pi` / `omp` coding agent published from github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi. The postinstall script install.cjs instead downloads a platform-specific prebuilt executable from https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v<version>/<asset>, an unrelated GitHub organization with no declared relationship to the stated publisher. The downloaded bytes are chmod 0755'd (no hash or signature verification) and staged into node_modules/@apexfdn/apex/bin. The bin wrapper apex.cjs then invokes the downloaded binary with the user's argv and full process.env on every CLI invocation. The declared `main` points into a `src/` directory that is not shipped in the tarball, so the package has no library behavior of its own — its only effect is to fetch and run an opaque native binary from a third-party org. Whoever controls Apex-Foundation/copilot releases controls what code runs on every installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
